Therefore, you must always return a legal move string. # Required API The provided python file must implement the following API: ```python def policy(pieces: dict[str, str], to_play: str, legal_moves: list[str], memory: dict) -> tuple[str, dict]: ... ``` # State Representation - `memory` is an empty dictionary that you may use however you want to store information between calls. - You may use and store anything in `memory` and store any keys and values you want (even leave it empty). - You are always the player whose turn it is (given by `to_play`). - `pieces` is a dictionary mapping squares to piece codes, e.g. `{'e1': 'bK', 'f3': 'wR'}`. - Squares are in algebraic coordinates: file `a`-`h` and rank `1`-`8` (e.g. `'e4'`). - Piece codes are two characters: color + piece type. - Colors: `'w'` = White, `'b'` = Black. - Piece types: `K` King, `Q` Queen, `R` Rook, `B` Bishop, `N` Knight, `P` Pawn. - `to_play` is either `'white'` or `'black'`. - `legal_moves` is the complete list of legal moves for the side to play, represented as chess move strings. # Action / Return Format - Return a tuple `(action, memory)` where `memory` is a dictionary that you will receive next call (You may return an empty dictionary if you don't want to store anything). - `action` is a move string that is an element of `legal_moves`. - Do not return any extra text, commentary, or formatting—only the move string. - The move strings may include captures (`x`), check (`+`), promotions (`=Q`, `=R`, `=B`, `=N`), castling (`O-O` / `O-O-O`), disambiguation (e.g. `Nec3`), and checks/mates. - Example format of `legal_moves` you might receive: - `['Ra1', 'c3', 'c4', 'Be4', 'Bxf5', 'Bxb5', 'Bc4', 'Kd2', 'Nec3', 'Ng1', 'f4', 'Rf1', 'Rg1', 'h3', 'h5', 'hxg5', 'O-O', 'Kf3', 'Kf4', 'b8=B', 'b8=N', 'b8=Q', 'b8=R']` - Your goal is to choose the strongest move under standard chess objectives: prioritize checkmate if available;
